subject: ent
title: Sensorineural hearing loss and inner ear disorders

steps.tx: **Sensorineural loss** sits in the cochlea or the auditory nerve, so air and bone thresholds fall together with no gap. The **Weber test** points to the better ear while Rinne stays positive, the mirror of conductive disease. Speech discrimination suffers beyond pure loudness, with recruitment and **tinnitus** as companions. Tuning forks can mislead in dead ears without masking, so audiometry with speech scores grades and lateralises disease.
steps.say: Sensorineural loss sits in the cochlea or the auditory nerve, so air and bone thresholds fall together with no gap between them. The Weber fork points to the better ear while Rinne stays positive on both sides. Speech clarity suffers more than loudness, with abnormal loudness growth and ringing as companions. Tuning forks can mislead in a dead ear unless masking is used. Formal audiometry with speech scores grades the loss and identifies the side.

steps.tx: **Meniere disease** brings episodic vertigo lasting minutes to hours with fluctuating low tone loss, **tinnitus**, and fullness in one ear from **endolymphatic hydrops**. Attacks cluster and then burn out, leaving progressive deafness. Care climbs from lifestyle measures with betahistine or diuretics through intratympanic therapy to surgery for disabling vertigo, while bilateral disease limits destructive options.
steps.say: Meniere disease brings attacks of spinning that last minutes to hours with fluctuating deafness, ringing, and fullness in one ear. The cause is excess fluid pressure in the inner ear chamber. Attacks cluster for years and then burn out, leaving progressive hearing loss. Care starts with lifestyle measures with betahistine or water tablets and rises through eardrum injections to surgery for disabling vertigo. Destructive options remain unsuitable when both ears carry the disease.

steps.tx: The cochlear section shows a distended **scala media** ballooning with endolymph and bowing Reissner membrane, the **hydrops** of Meniere disease, beside a normal inset. This matches the vertigo step where one ear suffers fluctuating low tone loss with fullness. In the exam, link episodic spinning of minutes to hours with unilateral **tinnitus**, and protect bilateral ears from destructive surgery.
steps.say: This cochlear section presents a swollen middle chamber ballooned with fluid that bows the thin membrane above it. The normal inset alongside shows how much the chamber has expanded. Such fluid pressure explains attacks of spinning with one sided deafness, ringing, and fullness. Attacks last minutes to hours and cluster before burning out. Destructive surgery remains forbidden when both ears carry the disease.

vis.alt: Cochlear cross section with distended endolymphatic scala media bowing Reissner membrane, organ of Corti, scala vestibuli and tympani, normal inset
vis.caption: Cochlear endolymphatic hydrops distending scala media in Menieres. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Sudden sensorineural loss** of 30 dB or more across three frequencies within days is an otologic emergency. Most cases are idiopathic or viral, but stroke and **acoustic neuroma** hide among them. Urgent audiometry with early **steroids** and MRI of the internal auditory meatus must follow without delay, since late treatment worsens recovery. Bilateral sudden deafness points to systemic, drug, or autoimmune causes instead.
steps.say: Sudden deafness of 30 decibels or more across three frequencies within days is an emergency of the ear. Most cases are idiopathic or viral, but stroke and nerve tumours hide among them. Urgent hearing tests with early steroids and a scan of the internal auditory canal must follow without delay. Late treatment worsens the chance of recovery. Deafness striking both ears together points to systemic, drug, or autoimmune causes.

steps.tx: **Vestibular schwannoma** grows slowly from balance nerve fibres in the cerebellopontine angle, causing one sided progressive loss with **tinnitus** and imbalance, then facial numbness or weakness when large. Bilateral tumours define **neurofibromatosis type 2**. Gadolinium MRI of the internal meatus confirms it, and care balances observation, radiosurgery, or microsurgery against growth, hearing, and facial function.
steps.say: A vestibular schwannoma grows slowly from the balance nerve near the brainstem and causes one sided progressive deafness with ringing and unsteadiness. Large tumours press the trigeminal and facial nerves and produce numbness or weakness. Tumours in both ears indicate neurofibromatosis type 2. Gadolinium scanning of the internal auditory canal confirms the diagnosis. Care balances watchful waiting, focused radiation, or microsurgery against growth, hearing, and facial function.

vis.alt: Gadolinium-enhanced MRI of brain showing a brightly enhancing mass in the internal auditory meatus extending into the cerebellopontine angle, consistent with vestibular schwannoma.
vis.caption: MRI shows vestibular schwannoma in cerebellopontine angle. Image: see above, CC BY 2.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Ageing brings symmetric high tone **presbycusis**, while noise carves a notch at 4 kHz. Aminoglycosides and cisplatin kill outer hair cells from the base upward, so high frequencies fail first and need monitoring. Perilymph fistula and superior canal dehiscence produce vertigo triggered by pressure or loud sound. Autoimmune inner ear disease marches bilaterally over weeks but **steroids** can halt it, unlike most degenerative losses.
steps.say: Ageing produces symmetric loss of high tones that audiograms reveal in both ears. Noise exposure produces a characteristic notch at 4000 Hertz. Aminoglycosides and cisplatin destroy outer hair cells from the base upward, so high frequencies fail first and need monitoring during treatment. Leaks and canal dehiscence produce brief spinning triggered by pressure or loud sound. Autoimmune disease marches in both ears over weeks but often improves with steroids.
